problem: More people wanted coverage than there were places.
title: Oregon allocates Medicaid places by lottery
context: Oregon could only afford to add a limited number of low-income adults to its Medicaid programme.
decision_made: Draw names by lottery for the available places.
action_taken: Researchers compared lottery winners with non-winners.
observed_outcome: Winners were about 25 percentage points more likely to be insured, used more care, had lower medical debt and reported better health; depression fell but blood pressure, cholesterol and employment showed no significant effect in the first two years.
lessons: Insurance can improve access, finances and mental health quickly while measured physical health measures may take longer to move.
limitations: Results are specific to the population, plan and period. Only early findings were checked here.

claims.claim_text: Oregon used a lottery in 2008 to assign limited Medicaid places among applicants.
Lottery winners had higher coverage, more care use and lower medical debt in the first year.
